text:
ida: hitting a weird one in the kotlin sample app — cancel a Retrofit suspend streaming call, then the next request blocks for ~15-20s on Pixel 8 behind corp VPN. emulator fine. anyone seen keepalive/close_wait oddness? :thinking_face:
noah: sounds like socket half-close + VPN NAT. are you explicitly closing the ResponseBody when cancelling?
ida: we rely on coroutine cancellation; pattern is simple suspend retrofit call with no explicit close. snippet: `val r = api.stream(); // cancelled by nav away`
noah: tried that in local repro, cancelling coroutine doesn't always propagate to OkHttp Call. quick fix: wire `invokeOnCancellation { call.cancel() }` in suspend wrapper.
ida: added that and immediate followup requests stopped stalling. evictAll() reduced frequency but wasn't reliable.
infra-bot: Issue created: #9001 "suspend cancel -> socket reuse stalls on Pixel+VPN"
oliver: could be OkHttp HTTP/2 stream lifecycle on 5.x combined with platform TCP behavior. disabling keepAlive made it go away in my test but not acceptable.
noah: SDK mitigation idea: add a small Kotlin extension `suspendCancellableAsyncCall` that registers cancellation to cancel the call and add a builder flag `autoCancelOnCoroutineCancel` default off. document caveat in onboarding.
ida: i'll open a draft PR with the helper and a sampleapp example plus an instrumented test on Pixel 7/8 emulators. linking issue in PR. :raised_hands:
oliver: also recommend AuthInterceptor use a no-retry client for refresh calls (separate issue) — we saw dup POSTs when retry + blocking refresh overlap.
ida: good call. adding note to PR description. thanks all! :thumbsup:
